subject.title: feat(auth): support configurable session cookie names

question: Should ClickClack permanently expose a configurable session-cookie name and return the effective name from desktop OAuth consume?
rationale: This introduces an operator-facing authentication setting and a cross-version desktop/server API contract; tests cannot determine whether maintainers want that permanent surface.

options.title: Approve the contract
options.body: Keep the compatible default, document the reauthentication effect, and merge after packaged-desktop proof demonstrates the custom-name flow.

options.title: Limit it to browsers
options.body: Support server-side browser-session isolation but defer the desktop response contract until its compatibility model is separately approved.

options.title: Decline the setting
options.body: Retain the fixed cookie name and require separate hostnames or another deployment-level isolation mechanism.

recommendation.title: Approve the contract
recommendation.body: Keep the compatible default, document the reauthentication effect, and merge after packaged-desktop proof demonstrates the custom-name flow.

likelyOwner.reason: The v0.1.0 release provenance connects this person to the existing desktop OAuth and session-cookie security contract.
